questions.questionText: What is an example of the purchase of a consumer good?

options.text: A farm owner buys a television.
A farm owner buys additional land.
A farm owner buys fertiliser for their crops.
A farm owner buys some farming equipment.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the factors of production in an economy?

options.text: to make goods and services to fulfil wants and needs
to provide an even distribution of income
to provide tax income for the government
to reduce the existence of external costs

options.text: clear product information
high external costs
high product taxes
low customer demand

questions.questionText:
The wage of labour in a firm increases.
What is the most likely effect on the production process?

options.text: Capital replaces labour immediately.
Capital replaces labour in the long run.
Labour replaces capital immediately.
Labour replaces capital in the long run.

What is most likely to lead to an improvement in labour productivity in an industry?

options.text: an increase in capital investment
an increase in income tax rates
an increase in the demand for the industry’s product
an increase in the number of firms in the industry

questions.questionText: How is a government most likely to prevent the growth of monopolies?

options.text: by encouraging mergers in the private sector
by establishing nationalised industries
by promoting the benefits of economies of scale
by reducing barriers to entry into an industry

questions.questionText: What is not included in public expenditure?

options.text: capital spending by firms
interest payments on government borrowing
investment in defence by the central government
subsidies to bus companies from local government

questions.questionText: When is the budget described as balanced?

options.text: when direct taxes and indirect taxes are equal
when exports and imports are equal
when government spending and government revenue are equal
when the demand for money and the supply of money are equal

questions.questionText:
The government wishes to increase economic growth in its economy.
What would not be likely to achieve this aim?

options.text: The central bank encourages bank lending.
The central bank lowers interest rates.
The government increases sales tax (VAT).
The government subsidises new industries.

questions.questionText:
The government redistributes income more evenly.
What is most likely to increase?

options.text: the incentive to work
the level of savings
the need for welfare payments
the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: What may directly cause economic growth?

options.text: higher imports
higher levels of resources
higher taxation
higher unemployment

questions.questionText: What would not be required in the construction of an index of consumer prices?

options.text: the selection of a base year
the selection of a representative range of items
the calculation of average wage levels
the weighting of each item in the index

questions.questionText: What distinguishes a more developed country from a less developed country?

options.text: Inflation rates are higher in the more developed country.
Interest rates are higher in the more developed country.
Natural resources are higher in the more developed country.
Real incomes are higher in the more developed country.

questions.questionText:
An additional 700000 UK children and pensioners fell into relative poverty between 2013 and
2017.
What might be the reason for this?

options.text: Direct taxes had increased, and indirect taxes had fallen.
Real gross domestic product was rising faster than the population.
The death rate was exceeding the birth rate.
The real value of government welfare benefits had fallen.

questions.questionText: What is a quota in international trade?

options.text: a government grant to encourage production
an administrative and technical barrier
a limit on the quantity of imports
a tax on imports

questions.questionText:
Many low-income countries rely on exports of raw materials such as coffee or iron ore to earn
them foreign currency.
What is a disadvantage of this?

options.text: Countries have a constant demand for raw materials.
International trade only benefits the importing countries.
It is necessary for low-income countries to belong to a free trade area.
Raw materials have fluctuating prices.

questions.questionText: What is included as part of the current account of the balance of payments?

options.text: all government income and expenditure
money withdrawn from a bank account
investments in other countries by manufacturers
trade in goods and services
